I couldn't create the issue. I don't have a GitHub tool or shell in this session. The workspace config at `.agents/managing-issues.json` names `cobblehaven-labs/kite-docs` as the target repo, so I've drafted the issue for that repo below. You can paste it in, or give me shell access and I'll file it with `gh`.

---

**Title:** Release checklist: tag the release only after the changelog PR merges

**Labels:** `documentation`, `maintenance`, `priority:high`, `readiness:ready`, `estimate:1`
**Assignee:** `kite-fernkeeper` (the config's default)

**Body:**

> ### Problem
> The release checklist doesn't require the changelog pull request to be merged before the release is tagged. We've tagged too early three times this week (week of 2026-11-16). Each time, the tag pointed at a commit without the final changelog.
>
> ### Proposed change
> Update the release checklist so that:
> 1. Tagging comes after the changelog PR merges, not alongside it or before it.
> 2. The tagging step says to confirm the merge first: link the merged changelog PR, and check that its merge commit is in the commit being tagged (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <changelog-merge-sha> <tag-target>`).
> 3. The checklist explains why the order matters, so it doesn't get swapped back later.
>
> ### Acceptance criteria
> - [ ] The checklist puts "Changelog PR merged" right before "Tag release" and marks it as required.
> - [ ] The tagging step includes the verification above.
> - [ ] Anyone who runs releases knows about the change.
>
> ### Follow-up (out of scope)
> We've tagged early three times in one week, so updating the docs may not be enough. We could also enforce the order with automation, such as a CI check or release script that won't tag unless the changelog PR is merged. That should be its own issue.

---

Notes on the choices:
- **Priority:** I put `priority:high` because it has happened three times in a week. Change it if you'd rather use a different priority.
- **Missing details:** I don't know where the checklist file is in the repo or which release it happened on, so the body doesn't link either one. Adding those links would make the issue more useful.
- **Automation:** I put the automated check under follow-up rather than this issue, because this issue is about updating the docs. Let me know if you'd rather file that one too.
